newsitem.title: GERMANY: Thyssen consolidates car supply business -report.
newsitem.headline: Thyssen consolidates car supply business -report.

text.p: German steel and engineering group Thyssen plans to reorganise its automotive components business, consolidating activities under the umbrella of the U.S.-based Budd Co, a magazine report said on Saturday.

The new division, to be called Thyssen-Budd Automotive GmbH, will include Thyssen's forging and shaping subsidiaries Thyssen Guss and Thyssen Umformtechnik, weekly Der Spiegel said in a report made available ahead of publication on Monday.
Thyssen was not immediately available for comment.
Budd, based in Troy, Michigan, employs around 10,000 people and has annual revenues of around 2.5 billion marks.
The new division will be based in Essen, Germany, and it will be led by Siegfried Buschmann, former head of Budd Co.
The merger of activities will boost the group's turnover to around 4.5 billion marks, making it Germany's third-largest car components supplier after Robert Bosch and Mannesmann, the report said.
